blocks.md:
When describing how a situation **changed due to circumstances, outside events, or time**, use **-게 되다** (*“turned out that... / came to do... / ended up doing...”*):

- *“한국 회사에서 일하**게 됐어요**.”* (I ended up working at a Korean company.)
- *“한국 친구 덕분에 김치를 좋아하**게 됐어요**.”* (Thanks to my Korean friend, I came to like kimchi.)

Unlike pure personal decisions (*-기로 했어요*), **-게 되다** emphasizes the result of changing circumstances.

blocks.md:
Have you wondered why Koreans say **맛있게 드세요** instead of 맛있다?

Attaching **-게** to an adjective stem turns it into an **adverb** (*“-ly / in a ~ manner”*):
- **맛있다** (delicious) → **맛있게** (deliciously / enjoyably)
- **따뜻하다** (warm) → **따뜻하게** (warmly)
- **예쁘다** (pretty) → **예쁘게** (prettily / nicely)
- **재미있다** (fun) → **재미있게** (enjoyably / with fun)

Simply take the stem and add **-게**!

blocks.q: Before eating together, how do you politely tell someone "Enjoy your meal"?
blocks.why: 맛있게 modifies 드세요: 맛있게 드세요! (Eat deliciously / Enjoy your meal!).

blocks.meaning: Because the weather is cold, please dress warmly.

blocks.q: Match adjectives with their adverb forms:

blocks.hint: Change 맛있다 into an adverb modifying 드세요: 맛있- + -게 = 맛있게
blocks.why: Adverb form is 맛있게: 음식을 맛있게 드세요.

blocks.q: Please dress warmly because it is cold.

title.ko: 3강. 꼴 만들기: 부사 만들기 -게 와 관용 표현
title.en: Lesson 3. Forming Adverbs with -게 & Common Idioms

blocks.md:
Attaching **-게** to an adjective stem transforms it into an adverb meaning *“-ly”* or *“in a ... way”*:

- **크다 → 크게** *(loudly / largely)*: 음악을 **크게** 틀었어요.
- **쉽다 → 쉽게** *(easily)*: 시험문제를 **쉽게** 풀었어요.
- **예쁘다 → 예쁘게** *(prettily / nicely)*: 머리를 **예쁘게** 잘랐어요.

Notice that **-게** attaches directly to the adjective stem without changing based on batchim! However, a few common adjectives have irregular or independent adverb twins: **많다 → 많이**, **빠르다 → 빨리**, **깨끗하다 → 깨끗이**.

blocks.why: 크다 becomes the adverb 크게 when modifying the action verb 말씀해 주세요: 크게 말씀해 주세요.

blocks.why: Attach -게 directly to the stem 편하- to form the adverb 편하게.

blocks.why: 짧다 (short) takes -게 to become the adverb 짧게 (cut my hair short).

title.ko: 4강. 헷갈리는 짝과 가르기: -게 되다 vs -기로 하다
title.en: Lesson 4. Circumstance vs Decision: -게 되다 vs -기로 하다

blocks.h: Circumstance (-게 되다) vs Personal Decision (-기로 하다)
blocks.md:
Both expressions talk about changes in situation or future actions, but who decided it?

1. **-게 되다**, **Circumstance / External change** (*“Turned out that...”*, *“Came to...”*).
   - The result happened naturally, unexpectedly, or due to external factors (like company orders or luck).
   - 회사 발령으로 부산에 살**게 됐어요**. *(I ended up living in Busan due to company relocation)*

2. **-기로 하다**, **Personal resolution / Mutual appointment** (*“Decided to...”*).
   - The speaker actively chose to do this action.
   - 부산으로 이사 가**기로 했어요**. *(I personally decided to move to Busan)*

Focus
Example

blocks.why: -게 되다 emphasizes that the event was brought about by circumstances outside purely personal choice: 일하게 되었어요.

blocks.meaning: Thanks to my friend, I came to know about a great book.
blocks.why: 알게 되다 expresses coming to know something over time or through circumstance.

blocks.q: 살다 (to live) / Express that you ended up living in Seoul: 「회사 일 때문에 서울에서 ___ . (came to live)」
blocks.why: Attach -게 되다 to the stem 살- → 살게 되다 (past polite: 살게 되었어요 / 살게 됐어요).

blocks.q: A: "그 노래는 어떻게 알았어요?" How do you naturally explain: "I happened to hear it at a café"? (듣다 = to hear)
blocks.why: 우연히 (by chance) perfectly pairs with -게 되었어요 to describe a natural occurrence: 듣게 되었어요.

blocks.say: 좋은 기회가 생겨서 한국에서 일하게 되었어요.
